clue.text: Slater maybe gets into difficulties without the boss

indicators.note: gets into tells us the shuffled letters go inside the word for difficulties

parts.note: being in a mess is being in difficulties

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the word Slater are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A roofer finds himself in trouble with no employer to answer to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns SLATER into ASTERL, and 'gets into' puts those letters inside MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no master means having no employer or boss over you.

clue.text: A thinker to shrink from

explanation.surface: A philosopher reluctant to face something.
explanation.definitionFit: A great intellect is called a fine mind, and to object to or recoil from something is to mind it.

clue.text: Not involved — not backing up the fool

parts.note: something not involved is uncomplicated, plain

indicators.note: backing up in a down clue means the word not is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word not taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of it and refuses to support a foolish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns NOT into TON, which goes after SIMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a dim-witted person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: An ancient wood

explanation.surface: A very old forest.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is an older person, a senior, and the elder is a shrub or small tree whose timber is a wood.

clue.text: Catches girls with nothing inside them

indicators.note: inside them says the nothing letter goes within the word for girls

parts.note: lasses is a Scots and northern word for girls
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone takes hold of young women who have empty heads.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope, so lassoes means catches.

clue.text: Spread awful scare about not drinking

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the teetotal abbreviation
awful hints the word scare comes out badly mangled

parts.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, describes someone not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A terrible fright spreads round a group of abstainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges SCARE as SCAER, and 'about' wraps those letters round TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter seed is to spread it widely, the two verbs being synonyms.

clue.text: Avoid editing a missing poet

indicators.note: editing suggests the word Avoid is being reworked into a new order
missing says one letter, the a, has gone from the reworked word

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid revising a poem by a poet who has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AVOID, shuffled ('editing') with the A 'missing', leave the four letters of the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Some clever new writer of science-fiction

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bright new author of science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, an early classic of the genre.

clue.text: Having words-it's an undisciplined Lower House!

indicators.note: undisciplined suggests the letters of the preceding words run riot into a new order

parts.note: the letters of words and it's, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy lower parliamentary chamber where members argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower House' sounds like a parliament, but it means the lower floor of a house; the wit lies there.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground floor of a home, below the stairs, is its lower part.

clue.text: The man willing to have a go at the alternative

parts.note: having a go at something is giving it a test or trial
taken as written
or introduces the alternative choice

explanation.surface: A man ready to attempt the other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' reads as eager, but here it means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a legal will, so one engaged in willing.

clue.text: This drifter isn't crazy

parts.note: isn't, as a denial, gives no
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A wanderer who is perfectly sane.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place with no fixed home, like a drifter.

clue.text: The shabby fellow in the field will frighten one of the birds

definitions.text: The shabby fellow in the field

parts.note: to scare is to frighten
the crow is a common bird

explanation.surface: A ragged man in a meadow will startle a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw figure in old clothes stands in farmland to keep birds off the crops.

clue.text: Make declaration without thought to dim solicitor

parts.note: to blur is to dim or make indistinct
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: Someone speaks rashly to a stupid lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer and 'dim' a stupid one; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak suddenly and tactlessly is to say something on impulse, unthinkingly.

clue.text: A theatre's stage-door has such a lock

indicators.note: has says the phrase before it holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A theatre's stage entrance is fitted with a particular kind of lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Hand one over at one point, being enthusiastic

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
the Roman numeral for one is I
on can mean over, as in a blanket on the bed
taken as written
E is east, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone passes a thing on at a certain moment, full of eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fervent and keen about something is passionate about it.

clue.text: Account 13 essential for the thespian

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A vital bookkeeping record for a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer on stage is a thespian, after Thespis, the first Greek actor.

clue.text: Raising rice, note yield

indicators.note: yield, in the sense of give way, says the letters of rice and note bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer records the output of the rice harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a building is putting it up, the act of construction.

clue.text: In tears, moved by drink

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the words In tears are shifted around

explanation.surface: Someone weeping with emotion over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like emotion to go with tears; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Following one child around at four

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: around says the word for child is wrapped round the letters that follow

parts.note: a mite is a small child
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone trailing a youngster at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' splits MITE as MIT...E around ATIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying or following another's example is imitative behaviour.

clue.text: Start sprouting if not lacking natural light

indicators.note: Start points at the first letter of the word sprouting

parts.note: unless means if not

explanation.surface: A gardener's tip: seeds begin to grow only if they get daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with no sunshine is dark, deprived of daylight.

clue.text: Coastal area which sets the South-east apart

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
aside means apart, to one side

explanation.surface: A stretch of coast that makes England's south-east distinct.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the land by the sea, a coastal region visited on holiday.

clue.text: A bothersome dog?

parts.note: a breed of hound used for hunting hares, whose name also describes one who pesters or harasses

explanation.definitionFit: This hunting hound's name also means one who harries, pestering someone persistently.

clue.text: They provide capital cover!

parts.note: capital is read as the head, from Latin caput, so the cover is headgear and the makers are those who sell it

explanation.definitionFit: Milliners and similar tradesmen make and sell headgear, cover for the head.

clue.text: Go round or part

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: An instruction to circle or to split up.
explanation.definitionFit: To circle around a planet is to travel in a path round it.

clue.text: Making a scholar study a philosopher

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: How a student becomes a thinker by learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman of the scientific method.

clue.text: Absolute monarch at a court occasion

indicators.note: occasion, in the sense of bring about, says the letters of at a court are made into something new

explanation.surface: A despotic ruler attends a royal function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasion' reads as an event at court; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with unlimited power is a despot, an absolute sovereign.

clue.text: A level hundred pounds will go on dope

indicators.note: will go on says the letters before it sit on top of the next word in this down clue

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds
an ass is a dope, a fool

explanation.surface: An exam pass costing a hundred pounds will be spent on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A level' looks like the British school exam, but it means a rank or grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a rank or grade, as in first-class travel.

clue.text: This is considered material

explanation.surface: Something regarded as relevant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: If you believed or judged something you felt it, and felt is also a matted woollen fabric.

clue.text: Retired man finding an object in routine work

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the object goes inside the word for routine work

parts.note: a chore is a routine domestic task
it is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: A pensioner discovers a thing in his daily tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests a pensioner, but it means withdrawn from the world, a hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse who has withdrawn from society.

clue.text: An article to enjoy all the same

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to like is to enjoy

explanation.surface: A thing to enjoy regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Things identical or similar are all the same as each other.

clue.text: She's English and coming back

indicators.note: coming back says the word and is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who is English is returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns AND into DNA, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's first name, so the pronoun she stands for it.

clue.text: Its present form is lasting well

indicators.note: form suggests the letters of its present take on a new shape

explanation.surface: Its current shape will endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring or that keeps going without fading is long-lasting.
